findings.detail: The comment on this line states the intent plainly — "a silent pause looks like a hang" — but `addLog` is the only surface the notice reaches. `App.tsx:136` initialises `showLogs` to `false`, and the only `aria-live` region in App.tsx (line 124) is the lazy-tab loading fallback, not the log list. During an overload the user now sees `ProgressBar` (TranslateTab.tsx:963) frozen at its last value with the static label `Processing (Batch: N)` for up to 120s of new waiting — exactly the scenario this PR exists to handle — with nothing on screen explaining it, and nothing announced to a screen reader. The information exists; it is just behind a drawer the user has no reason to have opened. Not higher severity because the run still completes or exports a correct `PARTIAL_` file either way, and the bound is 120s rather than indefinite. It would be medium if the wait were unbounded or if it also suppressed the existing error reporting.
findings.summary: Overload wait is announced only in a log drawer that is collapsed by default

findings.detail: `services/geminiService.ts:3-7` documents the convention explicitly — "`ModelNotice` is imported, not redeclared here: it is part of the provider contract" — and imports `AiTier`, `ApiKeyStatus`, `IAiService`, `ModelNotice` from this file. The new `OverloadBudget` interface goes the other way: it is declared at `services/geminiService.ts:466` and its shape is written out a second time here as `{ remainingSeconds?: number }`. `onRetryWait?: (message: string) => void` on line 61 is likewise a hand-copy of `ModelNotice`, which is defined on line 27 of this very file as exactly that signature. Nothing is broken today — the shapes are structurally identical, so the call in `TranslateTab.tsx:306` type-checks — but the two declarations can now drift silently: add a field to `OverloadBudget` and the contract keeps describing the old shape, with no compiler error anywhere. That is the drift the file's own convention was written to prevent.
findings.summary: `OverloadBudget` declared in the provider, then re-spelled inline in the contract
